title: Make a projection in real space (no FFT)
summary: Rotate the volume by ZYZ Euler angles, then sum along one axis to form the projection. No Fourier transform allowed.
prompt:
On the canvas: a 3D helix `volume` and a projection `projection` taken from some viewing direction. Produce an image matching `projection` without using any Fourier-domain nodes.

**Goal:** NCC ≥ 0.9 with `projection`.
hint:
`projection` was built by rotating the volume by SPIDER ZYZ Euler angles (phi, theta, psi) and summing along +z (= the body of `recon.pj3q`). Two real-space nodes do the job:

  volume → geom.rotate3d(phi=?, theta=?, psi=?) → recon.sum_axis(axis=z)

Strategy: inspect the wavy structure of `projection` to estimate how much the volume was tilted. Try theta = 0 / 30 / 60 / 90 and see which matches. Preview with `recon.vol_slice` or `recon.slice3d` to peek at the rotated volume.
